stories.headline: Brazil heads to an Oct. 25 runoff after Flávio Bolsonaro edges Lula but falls short of a majority
stories.summary: Brazil’s presidential race is going to a second round. The electoral court said neither Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, the 45-year-old Trump ally and son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, nor President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, cleared the 50% needed to win outright on Sunday; with nearly all votes counted, Bolsonaro had just over 55.8 million votes to Lula’s nearly 53.2 million, and the runoff is set for Oct. 25. “Brazil wants change… It’s the end of the Workers’ Party era,” Bolsonaro told supporters outside his Brasília home. Lula called the result “unexpected” and said, “Tomorrow we start a new campaign… I am very good in the knockout stage.” Ronaldo Caiado and Renan Santos, two candidates who drew moderate support, have said they will not endorse either man, and the winner takes office Jan. 5, 2027.

stories.headline: Yemen’s government launches an all-out offensive to retake Houthi territory as the Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Aramco
stories.summary: Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government said Sunday it is launching a major military campaign to recapture every area held by the Iran-backed Houthis, with President Rashad al-Alimi vowing to press on “until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia.” As the announcement came, the Houthis said they fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais, claiming major fires, in response to what they called 50 Saudi-led strikes in 12 hours. The Houthis seized the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and about 90 miles of Red Sea coast in a surprise offensive last month and have been pushing toward the last road between Taiz and Aden. Reuters sources say the Saudis will lead the air war with Yemeni forces on the ground, and the U.S. is already providing intelligence.

stories.headline: FBI arrests an Irvine realtor at LAX, accused of spying for China on the Taiwanese president’s son
stories.summary: Federal agents arrested Wanying “Heather” Zhang, a 34-year-old realtor from Irvine, California, at Los Angeles International Airport on Sunday as she was about to board a flight to Shanghai, charging her with acting as an unregistered agent of a foreign government. An FBI complaint says Zhang and an accomplice flew to Seattle in September 2025, rented a car, and photographed the suburban home and family of a top Taiwanese official; law enforcement sources told CBS News the target was Ting-Yu Lai, son of Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te. Neighbor security video allegedly shows the pair “appearing to film” him, his wife and child, and Zhang allegedly texted her handler, “Saw him… I am videorecording,” along with two license plate numbers. The FBI agent wrote that such pictures could give Beijing leverage over Taiwan’s president in a conflict.

stories.headline: Suspected ShinyHunters hacker tied to the FBI website breach is detained in Jordan and cooperating
stories.summary: Jordanian authorities detained Saif al-Din Khader this week, and the suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group is cooperating with investigators, two U.S. officials and another source told CBS News. ShinyHunters claimed last month that it defaced the FBI’s website and stole 2 to 3 terabytes of data on FBI workers through an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability, a claim that has not been publicly verified. The FBI declined to comment on the arrest but said it has “already worked with partners to arrest multiple subjects” and “will spare no resource” in the case. A 24-year-old Amsterdam man, identified by sources as Pepijn van der Stap, was already in Dutch custody days before the group announced the FBI hack; ShinyHunters says he has “no association” with it.

stories.headline: Two killed and 35 hurt as gunfire erupts at a Georgia homecoming block party
stories.summary: Two men, ages 20 and 23, were killed and 35 other people were injured early Sunday when shots rang out at a homecoming block party on Pine Street in Vienna, Georgia, about 50 miles south of Macon. Dooly County deputies on patrol heard the gunfire around 1:25 a.m.; more than 1,000 people had gathered, at least 50 shots were fired at two spots about a block apart, and some people were hit by cars as drivers scrambled to get away. Twenty-five of the injured were hospitalized. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation has joined the case, and authorities had not released any information about a suspect or motive as of Sunday evening.

stories.headline: Justice Alito says he considered retiring this year but stayed because ‘I can still make a contribution’
stories.summary: In a rare television interview with CBS News’ Jan Crawford, Justice Samuel Alito, 76, said he thought about retiring earlier this year but decided to stay: “I think I can still make a contribution.” He said the politics of who controls the Senate was not a factor, because “it’s too hard to predict what the political situation will be.” Alito, promoting his first book, So Ordered, called the image of him as angry or bitter “a caricature,” pointed to the court’s record on free speech, religious liberty and equal treatment regardless of race, and said the 2022 leak of his Dobbs draft “cast a pall over the Court” and “made us targets for assassination.”

stories.headline: Thune says Schumer ‘lives in fear’ of socialists taking over the Democratic Party
stories.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune said on “My View with Lara Trump” that Minority Leader Chuck Schumer “lives in fear” of the Democratic Party’s far-left wing. “I think he lives in fear of that every day. I really do,” Thune said, arguing that after Schumer once voted to reopen the government “it just got blown up by the far left. And ever since then… they defer to that far-left base.” He said Democrats have blocked traditionally bipartisan bills, including taking up the defense authorization, and that if Republicans keep both chambers in November, “the sky’s the limit” on military funding, judges and permitting reform. The remarks come after several primary wins by candidates backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani; Schumer’s office did not immediately respond.

stories.headline: Federal judge rules a warrantless Flock license-plate search was ‘indiscriminate mass surveillance’
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Sara Hill ruled that a Tulsa County, Oklahoma, sheriff’s deputy violated a woman’s Fourth Amendment rights by searching the Flock Safety license-plate camera network for her car without a warrant, when he had “no apparent reason” beyond its California plate. The deputy used her Flock travel history to justify searching the car, where he allegedly found 91 pounds of meth, but Hill ordered that evidence suppressed as “fruit of a poisonous tree.” She wrote that Flock “is a type of indiscriminate mass surveillance” that catalogs every passing vehicle and serves it up to police on demand. The ruling is not binding precedent but is one of the first federal findings that a Flock search was unconstitutional, as a number of towns and states drop the cameras.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones set a Russian fighter-jet base ablaze 300 miles from the front
stories.summary: Ukrainian strike drones hit the Khanskaya military airfield near Maykop in Russia’s Republic of Adygea early Sunday, sparking a large fire confirmed by NASA’s satellite fire-tracking data and geolocated video. Residents said the attack started shortly after 1 a.m. and went on for hours amid air-defense fire. The base, about 500 kilometers (roughly 300 miles) from Ukrainian-held territory, hosts Su-34 and Su-35 jets and serves as a refueling and logistics hub for Russian aircraft that fire missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine. Kyiv Post said it was the second long-range Ukrainian strike on major Russian aviation and launch sites within 24 hours.

stories.headline: Phil Collins calls Trump ‘nasty’ and teases a song about America titled ‘Fat People with Guns’
stories.summary: Asked by Piers Morgan what he thinks of President Trump, Phil Collins, 75, said “not a lot,” adding, “His whole manner is unattractive… when someone like Trump is as nasty as he is, you end up feeling dislike for him.” The Genesis drummer and singer, weeks away from his Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction as a solo artist, also said he has a song “waiting to be written called ‘Fat People with Guns,’ which is about America,” and that it would not surprise him if Trump tried to “overrule the two-term deal,” even as he called himself “not a political person.” Trump said in August that he would love to run again but “the law is very strong.” The White House did not immediately respond.

stories.headline: EU’s Oct. 6 meeting on Tesla FSD won’t include a vote, pushing any Europe-wide approval to December
stories.summary: Tesla had pointed to Oct. 6 as a possible EU-wide vote on its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system, but the agenda for the EU’s Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles now lists only continued discussion of the Dutch request, with 25 minutes set aside. The committee’s next meeting is in December, the earliest apparent chance for a bloc-wide decision. The Netherlands gave provisional approval in April, and Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia and the Czech Republic have recognized it, but those seven countries cover only about 12% of the EU population, short of the 15 states and 65% needed; Germany, France, Italy and Spain have not signed on. Safety groups object to FSD speed-offset settings, while Tesla says more than 70,000 European customers use FSD and it has had 4.1 times fewer collisions, a figure not independently verified.

stories.headline: SpaceX set to launch 21 Space Force data-relay satellites from Vandenberg early Monday
stories.summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 is scheduled to lift off from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 4:17 a.m. Eastern Monday with 21 Northrop Grumman-built satellites for the Space Force’s Space Development Agency. The Tranche 1 Transport Layer A mission is the fourth to send production satellites into the military’s Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture, a constellation meant to support missile tracking and secure communications for U.S. forces and allies. Booster B1103 is flying for the sixth time and is set to land at Landing Zone 4 less than 7.5 minutes after liftoff, which would be the 668th Falcon booster landing. The launch is one of 23 national security missions awarded to SpaceX.

stories.headline: Canon EOS R8 Mark II gets a firm Amazon delivery date of Oct. 21 at $1,899
stories.summary: Buyers waiting on Canon’s new compact full-frame camera now have a date: Amazon lists the EOS R8 Mark II for release on Oct. 20, with Prime delivery on Wednesday, Oct. 21, and the body at $1,899 sold and shipped by Amazon. Canon had only promised “late October,” though its own store now shows an estimated Oct. 20 arrival. The R8 Mark II keeps a 24.2-megapixel sensor but adds 5-axis in-body stabilization rated up to 7.5 stops at the center with compatible lenses, which the magazine calls probably the most important practical upgrade over the original R8.

stories.headline: SepticFlesh guitarist Christos Antoniou breaks ribs in a fall and will miss the start of the North American tour
stories.summary: Greek symphonic death metal band SepticFlesh will be shorthanded on its fall North American run after lead guitarist Christos Antoniou fractured and broke ribs in a fall. In a statement Sunday, the band said it will take the stage as a three-piece while he recovers, with the aim of having him rejoin later on the tour. The run with Arch Enemy, The Black Dahlia Murder, Crypta and Thrown Into Exile opens Oct. 5 in Riverside, California, and reaches New York’s Palladium Times Square on Oct. 24 and the Palladium in Worcester, Massachusetts, on Oct. 28.

stories.headline: Trumbull Center project approved: two-story shops-and-apartments building across from the firehouse
stories.summary: Trumbull has approved a new two-story mixed-use building at 855–861 White Plains Road, across from the Trumbull Center firehouse, with shops and restaurant space on the ground floor and 10 one-bedroom apartments upstairs, according to Sunday’s Trumbull Patch roundup. The project adds sidewalks, bike racks and electric-vehicle chargers, but two existing homes will be demolished once their residents relocate. Construction is expected to start next year and take about a year.
